o.text:
Inherited from Proto-Oghuz اَمْ (am), from Proto-Turkic *am. Cognate with Turkish and Turkmen am.
Related to amcıq with the same sense and derived from the same root.
Borrowed from Turkish uluslararası. By surface analysis, izafet II compound of uluslar + ara. First attested in 2021.
Ultimately from Arabic السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (as-salāmu ʕalaykum, “may peace be upon you”).
Morphologically from yan + -ğın. Cognate with Turkish yangın, Turkmen ýangyn, Crimean Tatar yanğın, Uzbek yong'in, Tatar янгын (yanğın), Bashkir янғын (yanğın).
From dala- (“bite”) + -ş. Cognate with Turkish dalaşmak. Compare to talischirmen (“I fight”) in the Codex Cumanicus.
Borrowed from Arabic أَرْبَاب (ʔarbāb), plural of رَبّ (rabb).
